children.text: tvaṃ ruṣṭā mayi cen namāmi bhavatīṃ neyaṃ tvayā namyatāṃ
namyatvaṃ tvayi bhāti pārthivatayā manye mahārājavat /
children.translated_text: the quality of being bowed to befits you, being a princess; I consider [it fitting] as for a great king.'
'If you are angry with me, I bow to you.' 'This bowing should not be done by you —

children.text: kumbhādiṣv ativartanāt tvaduditaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ sādhanaṃ
vāgvādeṣv iti nirjito dayitayā rāmaḥ sukhaṃ rātu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus defeated by his beloved in [logical] debates — may <s>Rāma</s> grant you happiness!
'Since it extends to pots and the like, the reason you have stated is common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) [i.e., inconclusive].'

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ puṣṇātu saukhyaṃ sumukhi sumukhatāṃ yāhi yāhi priyāṃ tām
anyāsaktaṃ kuto māṃ kalaṣasi dayite kevalaṃ tvatsvabhāvāt /
children.translated_text: 'Why do you falsely accuse me, attached to others? O beloved, it is merely your nature!'
May <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> foster [your] happiness! 'O beautiful-faced one, be of cheerful face! Go, go to that beloved one.'

children.text: yady evaṃ mugdhatā te karaṇam idam asādhāraṇaṃ pakṣamātre
vṛttatvād ity akasmāt praṇayakalahitāṃ rādhikāṃ sāntvayan vaḥ //
children.translated_text: since it applies [only to you].' Thus may he who unexpectedly pacified the love-quarreling <s>Rādhikā</s> [protect] you!
'If so, this innocence of yours is the cause — this is an exclusive reason (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>), occurring only in the thesis (<s>pakṣamātra</s>),

children.text: sarvaṃ vastu sukhāvahaṃ tava punaḥ kautaskutīyaṃ vyathā
kasmād evam udīryate jagad idaṃ yat tanmayaṃ bhāṣase /
children.translated_text: why do you speak thus, declaring this world to be full of that [suffering]?'
'Everything is a source of happiness for you; yet this inexplicable suffering —

children.text: hetus savyabhicāra eṣa virahāt dṛṣṭāntayor ity ayaṃ
saṃlāpas saha lakṣmaṇena viyujaḥ sītāpateḥ pātu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: May this conversation of the lord of <s>Sītā</s>, separated [from her], with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, protect you!
'This reason deviates (<s>savyabhicāra</s>) from separation, as seen in the two examples.'

children.text: bhīto 'haṃ virahī tuṣārakiraṇāt so 'yaṃ samujjṛmbhate
vijñātaḥ katham eṣa te mama yatas tāpaṃ karoty uccakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'How do you know this? Because it causes me intense torment.'
'I am afraid, being separated — the cool-rayed [moon] is rising.'

children.text: liṅgāt ko 'numinoti sādhyavirahavyāptād iyaṃ mugdhatā
mā bhaiṣīr iti pātu vo raghupatis saumitriṇā sāntvitaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Do not be afraid!' — may <s>Raghupati</s>, consoled by <s>Saumitri</s> (son of <s>Sumitrā</s>), protect you!
'From a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) — who would infer from one pervaded by the absence of what is to be proved (<s>sādhyavirahavyāpta</s>)? This is foolishness.'

children.text: kā bhītis tava candrato raghupate doṣākaratvād asāv
āsaktaḥ parapīḍane piśunavan naivaṃ kutaḥ kathyate /
children.translated_text: it is attached to harming others, like a slanderer.' 'Not so! Why is this said?'
'What fear of the moon do you have, O <s>Raghupati</s>?' 'Because it is the source of faults (<s>doṣākara</s>),

children.text: hetuḥ satpratipakṣa eṣa yad ayaṃ sadvṛttatāṃ gāhate
sodaryeṇa nirastabhīr iti sukhaṃ puṣṇātu vo rāghavaḥ //
children.translated_text: May <s>Rāghava</s>, whose fear was removed by his brother, protect you in happiness!
'This reason has a valid counter-argument (<s>satpratipakṣa</s>), since this [moon] practices good conduct.'

children.text: mithyeyaṃ virahavyathā tava mudaṃ datte purovartinī
māyāmaithilakanyakā priyatamābhāvena satyeva sā /
children.translated_text: she is indeed real, as the beloved.'
'This separation-pain of yours is false — the illusory <s>Maithilī</s> maiden standing before you gives delight;

children.text: ity uktaḥ sahajena sāntvanavidhau hetor amuṣyāśrayā
siddhatvaṃ pratipādayann avatu vaḥ śrījānakīvallabhaḥ //
children.translated_text: is unestablished (<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>) — may the dear lord of <s>Śrī Jānakī</s> protect you!
Thus addressed by his brother in the method of consolation, demonstrating that the substratum of this reason

children.text: cittaṃ me cittajanmā vidalayati śaraiḥ svāśrayaṃ nāśayet kaḥ
sthūlatvāc cetaso 'sau kim iva na kurute nirvicārapravṛttaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Because the mind is gross, what does that one, acting without discrimination, not do?'
'The mind-born one (<s>Manmatha</s>) shatters my mind with arrows — who would destroy his own support?'

children.text: āhuś ceto 'ṇumānaṃ katham iha bhavati sthūlatā tatsvarūpā
siddho 'yaṃ hetur evaṃ daśarathasutayoḥ pātu saṃbhāṣitaṃ vaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'This reason is [thus] established [to be unestablished in its own nature (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>)].' May this conversation of <s>Daśaratha</s>'s sons protect you!
'But they say the mind is atomic — how can grossness be its actual nature?'

children.text: vadhyetāṃ śukasāraṇau na hi tayor vadhyatvam asty eva tat
rakṣastvād daśakandharādivad ayaṃ hetus sahopādhikaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Because they are <s>rākṣasas</s>, like <s>Daśakaṇṭha</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) and others — this reason is conditional (<s>sopādhika</s>).'
'Let <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s> be killed! Their being worthy of death is indeed established.'

children.text: sadrohatvam upādhir atra sugamaḥ śeṣas tvayā cintyatām
ity ādityasutoktikhaṇḍanakaraḥ śrīrāghavaḥ pātu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: May <s>Śrī Rāghava</s>, who refuted the statement of the Son of the Sun (<s>Sugrīva</s>), protect you!
'Hostility (<s>sadrohatva</s>) is the easy condition (<s>upādhi</s>) here; the rest should be considered by you.'

children.text: jayyo rāghava eṣa mānuṣatayā tadbhakṣibhīr yātubhiḥ
naivaṃ bādhita eva hetur uditaḥ pratyakṣamānena hi /
children.translated_text: 'Not so — this reason is indeed contradicted (<s>bādhita</s>), [refuted] by the evidence of direct perception.'
'This <s>Rāghava</s> can be conquered because of his being human — by the man-eating <s>rākṣasas</s>.'

children.text: kva pratyakṣam idaṃ kharādinihatāv ity agrajasyāgrato
diśyāt tanmatabhidvibhīṣaṇasamudgītas sukhaṃ rāghavaḥ //
children.translated_text: may <s>Rāghava</s>, praised by <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> who shattered that doctrine, bestow happiness!
'Where is this [direct] perception?' — 'Since <s>Khara</s> and others have been slain...' — thus, before his elder brother,

children.text: ajñātvā hṛdgataṃ te katham abhilaṣitaṃ prārthaye bhāmini tvāṃ
nanv etasmāt kaṭākṣād anuminu hṛdaye rāga eveti cen na /
children.translated_text: 'From this sidelong glance, infer that there is passion in my heart!' — if so, no:
'Without knowing your heart's desire, how can I request you, O angry lady?'

children.text: hetus sopādhiko 'yaṃ bhavati gurutaro hrībharo 'sminn upādhiḥ
sādhyavyāpī priyādau sa khalu raṇamukhe sādhanāvyāpakaś ca //
children.translated_text: it indeed pervades the probandum (<s>sādhya</s>) in the beloved and such [contexts], but does not pervade the probans (<s>sādhana</s>) on the battlefield.
this reason is conditional (<s>sopādhika</s>) — the heavy burden of modesty (<s>hrī</s>) is the condition (<s>upādhi</s>) here;

children.text: koṭiliṃgapure vāsī yuvarājo mahākaviḥ /
children.translated_text: The crown prince, a great poet, dwelling in <s>Koṭiliṅgapura</s>,

children.text: hetvābhāsam udājahre daśaślokaiḥ satāṃ mude //
children.translated_text: has set forth the fallacious reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) in ten verses, for the delight of the good.
